note: What this archive did, in order, and what it had to take back. A family history that only shows its conclusions is asking to be believed on trust. This page exists so the reasoning can be checked — including the parts that were wrong.

entries.t: The tree, read
entries.w: A MyHeritage tree of 15,643 people, with the Booyzen line already seven generations deep and much of it citing Dutch Reformed registers and Cape probate. The job was never to find the family — it was to test what had been assembled, because a tree that good will be believed.

entries.t: Thirty-five documents transcribed
entries.w: Civil registrations, church registers, wills, a marriage allegation, a burial register and a gravestone — most of them images that had hung on the family tree for years without anyone reading them.

entries.t: The man was not shot by the British
entries.w: Willem Hermanus Booyzen died at Indwe on 13 September 1905 of an ulcer of the stomach, after fourteen months' illness, under a doctor's care. The testimony's central death is disproved for both candidates.

entries.t: The name caught changing on one sheet
entries.w: On the same 1905 form the registering clerk writes Booysen and the dead man's son signs Booyzen, four lines apart.

entries.t: WITHDRAWN — “two Barry sisters married Booysens”
entries.w: Asserted from a tree reading. John Barry's 1915 death notice lists only one, and the arithmetic closed exactly: eight surviving, two predeceased, one duplicate. Retracted on the page rather than quietly deleted.

entries.t: WITHDRAWN — the farm called “Armadale”
entries.w: An 1901 register was read as Armadale and a small argument about Scottish farm names was built on it. At full magnification on the original the word is ambiguous. The argument survives on Caerlaverock and Manorowen, which are certain; Armadale is gone.

entries.t: CORRECTED — “orphaned at seventeen”
entries.w: Written in four places, from a death date the archive had already corrected without propagating the change. Catherine was eighteen.

entries.t: CORRECTED — Anna Pretorius born 1906, not 1905
entries.w: Three documents beat the tree: the baptism register, her death form's age, and her marriage register's age with parental consent. A derived claim built on the wrong year was withdrawn with it.

entries.t: The 1820 Settler his family forgot
entries.w: George Augustus Kolbe — the Nautilus, Owen's party, Algoa Bay 1820 — whose grandson wrote “Father: Kolbe, thinks James was christian name. Mother: Unknown” with the man's carved headstone standing forty miles away.

entries.t: The Cape Rebel rolls searched, and the wrong surname noticed
entries.w: Twenty-six Booysens on the roll, every one Northern Cape. But the man in whose house the family married in July 1901 — D. W. Schoeman of Caerlaverock — was tried the month before. A note was written to search BARRY, and not acted on for some time.

entries.t: The Farm List result is VOID
entries.w: A negative result was recorded against Caerlaverock and Manorowen before checking what the register was. It is an Orange Free State land roll and was never going to hold a Cape farm. A control search on “Dordrecht” — 670 rebels, 0 farms — caught it.

entries.t: CORRECTED — my contradiction, not the tree's
entries.w: The archive flagged a conflict between the tree's 1827 death for James Montjoy and the 1840 date on his file. Both are right: he died in 1827 and the notice was filed thirteen years later. The error was mine.

entries.t: “Names of the Parents of the Deceased. Not Known.”
entries.w: Found by interpolating reference numbers across 2,223 images of an unindexed film. The oldest document in the archive, and it answers the question it was fetched to answer by refusing it.

entries.t: WITHDRAWN — the z as a family invention
entries.w: The archive had leaned on an 1879 signature. Then the 1851 register showed the clerk writing the godparents PIETERZEN in the same hand, and the Cape archives showed 39 documents under BOOYZEN with the earliest in 1779. The spelling was never invented. What survives is that this family switched between two spellings that both already existed.

entries.t: CORRECTED — Willem Hermanus is not a Booyzen name
entries.w: The archive had called it “a Booysen name crossing into the Mountjoys”. It is neither: it enters through Anna Catharina Slier's FIRST marriage, to a Pieterzen, and four generations carried a step-relation's name.

entries.t: The family is on the Cape Rebel roll — under Barry
entries.w: Acting at last on the note above. Fred J. Barry of Ivanhoe, Barkly East / Wodehouse, tried June 1901 — the same month as Schoeman; and Richard Peter Barry of Jerpoint, which is Kathleen Barry's brother's name. Identity unproven, district not.

entries.t: CORRECTED — a chart with five invented rows
entries.w: The first province chart drew nine provinces. The source reports four; I had filled in the rest to make the picture look complete. It now draws four, and a province the source does not report is a gap with a dash rather than a zero bar.

entries.t: A bug that removed exactly the names the archive knows best
entries.w: The ancestor chart rendered with names missing from half its boxes. The auto-linker was injecting HTML anchors into the SVG, where they do not render — so every person in the link index vanished from the chart while their dates stayed. It did not look broken; it looked plausible.

entries.t: CORRECTED — a search I reported as complete was not
entries.w: The archive stated that MOUNTJOY returned 42 documents in the Cape archives and that all 22 dated 1930 or later had been read. Twenty documents before 1930 were never opened. They include JAMES MOUNTJOY'S OWN WILLS of 1818 and 1827, and an 1834 Colonial Office memorial from his widow. A filter applied for convenience was reported as if it were the whole search.

entries.t: No death notice for Magdelena Elisabeth de Beer — twice over
entries.w: The Master's Office own index of death notices 1834–1912 was read on film at the “Beer, de” pages. She is not in it, which confirms the NAAIRS result from a second and older source.

entries.t: CORRECTED — the SANDF request was only half delivered
entries.w: Reported here as sent. It was sent, and one of the two addresses bounced: sandfdoc@mweb.co.za refused it at the server, 550 relay access denied. That is the address published almost everywhere for the Documentation Centre. The enquiry did reach archive@dod.mil.za, which has not replied. “Sent” and “delivered” are not the same word and this archive used the wrong one.

entries.t: Three documents identified that may break the oldest wall
entries.w: James Mountjoy's wills of 1818 and 1827, joint with Anna Catharina Slier, and an 1834 Colonial Office memorial from his widow. None digitised. A request went to the Western Cape Archives on 10 September 2026 — and unlike the last letter, delivery was checked.

entries.t: NARROWED — the 1905 sheet proves less than this archive said
entries.w: Seven Attorney-General files about one police constable at Middelburg, 1904–07, spell him BOOYSEN four times and BOOYZEN three — twice both ways inside 1905. So the clerk's Booysen on the 1905 death form is not an older spelling being displaced; it is what a Cape clerk might write on any day. What survives is the half that was always stronger: the son SIGNED, and chose the z.

entries.t: CORRECTED — the whole project searched one province out of nine
entries.w: Every NAAIRS search in this archive was run against the Cape depot. This family left the Cape about 1907 and the entire last generation died in Johannesburg, so their estates are in the Transvaal — and NAAIRS offers an “All Archives Repositories” database on the same selection page I used every time. BOOYZEN returns 39 in the Cape and 184 across all repositories. One hundred and forty-five documents unseen, including the estate files of nearly everyone in the last three generations.

entries.t: The Johannesburg generation's estates, found
entries.w: Anna Pretorius (1944), George Downing Mountjoy Booyzen (1947), John Barry Booyzen (1952), Henry James Booyzen (1956) — and Catharina Maria Sophia, the daughter baptised at Barkly Oost in 1891, who married a Daschner and died in 1946. Also two of the eight children on the 1863 death notice, and both sons of the second marriage.
